title: reservation-advisor-and-surge-signature-prober
author: Aisha Khan
description:
Context and motivation: We observed repeated burst-induced SLA pressure for medium-sized tenants in Dedicated pools where short spikes consumed available headroom and caused tail latency regressions. Existing autoscaler signals (95th util + simple buffer) react too slowly to sub-minute surges and do not account for variance observed in tenant request traces. This PR introduces two cooperating pieces: a lightweight Reservation Advisor that synthesizes a utilization-anchored reservation recommendation, and a Surge Signature Prober that produces high-frequency ‘surge fingerprints’ to let the advisor reason about short-tail burst risk.

Summary of changes: 1) controller/autoscaler: add ReservoirReservationAdvisor (configurable windowing + confidence bands) and an admission curve that blends steady-state reservation with short-lived surge buffers; 2) telemetry/exporter: add surge_signature histogram and a new nightly-sample exporter to surface per-tenant burst skew; 3) runtime/router: small admission hook to allow short soft-burst grants when advisor certifies low collision risk; 4) tests/docs: unit + integration tests for statistical sampling and a how-to in docs/dedicated/reservations.md.

Why this is different: Unlike our previous headroom heuristics, the advisor models both central tendency and burst skew using a reservoir sampler + exponential decay to weigh recent high-frequency signals. The Surge Signature Prober classifies patterns (spike, ramp, plateaus) and reports a compact signature that is cheap to compute (<200us per sample) and stable across languages. This enables faster preemptive soft grants and reduces reactive overprovisioning.

Checklist:
- [x] Implement Reservation Advisor controller and API surface
- [x] Implement Surge Signature Prober and telemetry hooks
- [x] Add unit tests for sampling and confidence bands
- [x] Add integration test that replays tenant burst traces (stress test)
- [x] Add docs section with configuration guidance and cost/latency tradeoffs
- [x] Run canary on staging and collect 48h telemetry

review_comments: Marco Diaz: Please ensure the advisor respects tenant-level max-reservation caps — otherwise we risk starving bursty tenants.
Aisha Khan: Added cap logic in reservoir_advisor.go and unit tests covering cap enforcement.
Leila Chen: The prober looks expensive in worst-case — can we make sampling conditional?
Aisha Khan: Sampling is gated by a lightweight rate limiter; added microbenchmark (<200us/sample) and documentation note.
Tom Bradshaw: CI flakes in integration test — looks like timing assumptions in the replay harness. Suggest switching to event-driven checkpoints.
Aisha Khan: Updated the harness to use explicit barriers and reduced timing fuzz; test stabilized locally and in CI.
release_notes: Introduce Reservation Advisor (utilization-anchored soft reservations) and Surge Signature Prober (high-frequency burst fingerprinting). New telemetry metrics (surge_signature, reservation_recommendation) and a docs guide for tuning reservation windows. Behavioral change: Dedicated autoscaler can grant short soft-bursts based on advisor confidence — default caps preserve tenant isolation.
notes_on_rollout: Rollout plan: 1) deploy advisor/prober binary behind feature flag (off by default) 2) enable per-pool in staging with conservative windows 3) monitor new surge_signature and reservation_recommendation panels for 72h 4) progressively enable soft-burst grants with a 1% initial traffic target and exponential ramp to 20% if no regressions seen.

ENG-4721: add opt-out API for tenants with strict billing constraints
